properties.description:
`orphan_node`'s repair note and the BL-199 self-host gate's failure text both name `governed_by(..., ruling: "parks")` as the second honest way on when a node's unattached state is deliberate, say plainly that deleting the node is the repair that looks clean and loses the most, and state the boundary: parking is read by `orphan_node` and the unsatisfied-requirement gap and by nothing else — it does not quiet `unthreaded_cluster` and does not cover the unproven-capability loop debt. The `link-artifacts` skill carries the same case for documents that correctly describe and implement nothing.

THE LIMIT IS PART OF THE CAPABILITY, not a caveat on it: a mechanism named without its scope produced the failure where a reporter found it, could not confirm it applied, and backed off.
properties.name: A structural finding names parking as the honest alternative, and names its limits
